subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the action items we discussed. If I missed anything, please flag it and I'll update.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Recent incidents where your in-house endpoint hit capacity during Black Friday-like traffic spikes, resulting in degraded model responses and increased latency for customer chat flows.
- Concern about single-region blast radius (primary cluster in us-west-2) and a lack of automated fallback to a different region or model variant.
- Lack of visibility into token-level latency/costs and per-route SLO tracking that would let SREs triage regressions faster.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend chat + proxy running on EKS (us-west-2)
- Custom cache layer for prompt prefixes and short-term KV cache
- Primary model: open-llm-large pinned in your infra; fallback is a smaller distilled model with manual switchovers
- Logging aggregated into ELK, no structured per-token tracing yet

Success criteria you're aiming for:
- Availability: 99.9% (with graceful degradation, not hard failures) for the customer-facing chat flows
- Latency: p50 < 200ms for quick interactions; p95 goals for longer LLM flows documented
- Clear, auditable fallback policy that triggers automatically on capacity/SLO breach (preferably region-aware)
- Cost target: avoid 3x-4x unit cost increases during peak by using automatic batching/caching and fallback model routing

Reliability & graceful degradation considerations we discussed:
- Incident history: you noted two significant incidents in the last 12 months where autoscaling failed under sudden bursts and manual failover took ~45 minutes.
- Fallback strategy: we talked about automatic routing to smaller quantized model variants and cross-region failover (primary in us-west-2, failover in us-east-1).
- SLO/SLA alignment: you're looking for tooling to instrument SLOs per route/model and for Redwood to support SLA language that maps to those SLOs during a trial.

Next steps (mutual action items):
- Redwood: send a short reliability playbook and SOC2 summary (attached) + a proposed MAD for a 30-day eval on a dedicated pool with cross-region routing enabled. (Jonas)
- Acme: share a high-level traffic profile (p50/p95 request sizes, concurrent sessions during peak) and any incident runbooks you'd want us to model. (Samantha)
- Schedule a technical call with your SRE and our SRE/infra lead to walk architecture and failover plan — proposed times below. (Jonas + Marissa)

Proposed times for SRE deep-dive (PT):
- Thu 19 Mar, 10:00–10:45
- Thu 19 Mar, 14:00–14:45

Attachments: redwood-reliability-playbook.pdf (summary), SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf

Thanks again — looking forward to the SRE call.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 18:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Thanks Jonas — this looks good and captures the conversation. A few clarifications and one request:

1) Incident details: the two incidents were Nov 2025 (30-minute outage due to autoscaler bug) and Jan 2026 (queue pile-up; we did a manual rollback to a smaller model which restored throughput after ~45 minutes). I can share the postmortems with the SREs on the call.

2) Fallback windows: we'd like automated fallback that preserves response quality (not every fallback is acceptable — some models produce hallucinations for policy responses). Can you confirm Redwood's approach to quality-preserving fallbacks?

3) For the SRE call, Thu 19 Mar 10:00 PT works for our team. Please send calendar invite and dial-in.

Appreciate the attachments — I'll review and share internally.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
Samantha.Lee@acmeretail.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Samantha — thanks for the details and the call confirmation. Quick answers and follow-ups below.

Quality-preserving fallbacks:
- Redwood’s routing policy supports weighted fallbacks and quality thresholds. We can define a fallback set that excludes model variants known to regress on policy prompts, and run a short eval against your policy prompt set during the trial. If a candidate fallback drops quality below an agreed threshold, we keep it out of the automatic failover path and only allow manual switchover.
- During the eval we'll generate per-prompt quality scores and share a matrix so your team can approve allowed fallbacks.

Technical notes for SRE deep-dive:
- We'll demonstrate cross-region routing (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover) with state-sync for the KV cache and show how prefix caching reduces load on origin.
- Proposal: run a 30-day eval on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with canary traffic + automatic fallback to smaller quantized models for non-policy-sensitive routes. Include tracing hooks so you get token-level latency breakdowns.

Attached are the reliability playbook and SOC2 summary. I’ll also upload the SRE deck to the drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-reliability-eval.

Action items we’ll take before the SRE call:
- Redwood: prepare an eval plan and a proposed MAD (mutual action document) that outlines success criteria, rollback points, and SLAs for the trial. (Jonas + Marissa)
- Acme: share traffic profile and policy prompt set (redacted as needed) so we can run the quality eval. (Samantha)

I’ll send the calendar invite for Thu 19 Mar 10:00 PT and include dial-in and Zoom link. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Jonas

Perfect — invite received and I confirmed with our SREs. We’ll upload the traffic profile and a redacted policy prompt set to the Drive folder by end of day.

A couple of quick asks for the SRE call:
- Please include any historical runbooks you recommend for automated failover so we can compare against our playbooks.
- If possible, bring an infra engineer who can speak to KV cache sync and replication behavior across regions.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Samantha
